title: Skill: Visual Editor
subtitle: A Figma-like Editor for Pages Built with AI Coding Agents
summary: A skill for AI coding agents: a Figma-like inspector that runs inside your page. Adjust it by hand, save real CSS.
body: When a page is built by talking to an AI coding agent, every change has to go through a text prompt — yet position, size and spacing are exactly what is hardest to put into words, and prose doesn't follow a designer's way of judging layout. Visual Editor is a skill that fills that gap: it installs a Figma-like inspector inside the page itself, so you drag, resize, retype and restyle live, then save real CSS in the units the author wrote. It loads only when the URL carries ?edit=1, so the shipped page is never touched.

sections.title:
“Drag it,
Don't describe it.”
sections.body: A Figma-like inspector that runs inside your page. Adjust it by hand, save real CSS.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.body: AI writes the page in one prompt. Then you spend an hour on the last 20%.

items.foot: Costs tokens. Loses precision at every hop.
Free. Exact. Then one save writes it all to CSS.

items.title: Judgement needs a visual loop
items.body: Nobody picks 15px over 16px by reading prose. You nudge, look, judge — and chat breaks that loop.

items.title: "A bit left" isn't a measurement
items.body: A drag says it exactly, in one second, for free. Words need a rebuild.

items.title: Handoff without translation
items.body: The agent builds it, the designer adjusts it in place. No annotated screenshots.

blocks.title: Three ways to fix the last 20%
blocks.note: Not a replacement for either — it covers the gap between them: the visual pass a designer has to make, without asking them to write code or spend an agent turn on every nudge.

sections.title: Capabilities
sections.body: Move, resize, retype, size type, scope, params, images — every edit happens on the page itself.

blocks.title: Point. Grab. Move.
blocks.body: Click to select, double-click to go deeper, drag to move. Where you drop it is where it goes.
blocks.alt: Selecting an element and dragging it to a new position

blocks.title: Eight handles. Resize.
blocks.body: Every side and corner is a handle. The badge shows real pixels; the CSS stays in `cqw` or `%`.
blocks.alt: Resizing an element by dragging its corner handle

blocks.title: Retype anything.
blocks.body: Double-click and type. Enter commits, Esc cancels, every keystroke is undoable.
blocks.alt: Double-clicking a headline and retyping it letter by letter

blocks.title: Size type by eye.
blocks.body: Step it until it looks right. A fluid `5.4 cqw` is still `cqw` when you're done.
blocks.alt: Stepping a headline's size up from the Typography panel

blocks.title: One card, or all seven.
blocks.body: Seven cards share a selector. Hover **All 7** to see the blast radius, or pick **Only this** — you always know which.
blocks.alt: Scope control: editing all seven cards, then only one

blocks.title: Every param, a real control.
blocks.body: Gradients, shadows, radius, fill, stroke, spacing — structured editors, not a CSS textarea.
blocks.alt: Editing gradient angle, adding a drop shadow, and rounding corners

blocks.title: Swap the artwork.
blocks.body: One button, your file picker, frame untouched. Works on `` and CSS backgrounds alike.
blocks.alt: Replacing an image element with new artwork

blocks.title: Hide it. Judge the page.
blocks.body: Toolbar in the way? Click the mark — it shuts to just the logo, red when hidden. Your edits keep working.
blocks.alt: Collapsing the toolbar into its logo and expanding it back
Opening the Save-as menu and exporting a CSS patch

items.title: Save
items.body: Writes the batch into your CSS overrides file. The page is just the page again.

items.title: Export CSS patch
items.body: Only the changes, with merge instructions in the header. A readable diff for review and handoff.

items.title: Export clean copy
items.body: The whole site, editor stripped out. What you ship.

blocks.title: One save, three shapes.
blocks.body: Edits pile up as a batch — the count rides on Save.

sections.title: Design Rules
sections.body: Four things it refuses to do — then two files and one loader to install it.

items.title: Look like AI made it.
items.body: No purple gradients, no glass blur. Hairlines, hard colours, square corners.

items.title: Rank its own controls.
items.body: Peers are equal-width and always there. Unavailable ones grey out in place.

items.title: Hide state.
items.body: Saved or dirty, open or shut — always visible, never a convention you must learn.

blocks.title: Two files. One loader.
blocks.body: Ask your agent to add it, or paste this yourself:
blocks.code:
<!-- before </body> — loads only when the URL carries ?edit=1 -->
<script>
  if (location.search.indexOf("edit=1") !== -1) {
    var css = document.createElement("link");
    css.rel = "stylesheet";
    css.href = "tools/visual-editor.css?v=18";
    document.head.appendChild(css);
    var js = document.createElement("script");
    js.src = "tools/visual-editor.js?v=18";
    js.defer = true;
    document.body.appendChild(js);
  }
</script>
